findings.rationale: Claim (issue_present): the last fallback in `definition_location` resolves a reference by BARE NAME over every workspace URI, in sorted-URI order, with no precedence for the current document and no owning-spec scoping (`.find(|symbol| symbol.name == reference.name)`). `index.definition_at(position)` only handles a cursor sitting on a declaration, so an ordinary local reference (e.g. `ready` inside `action flip()`) reaches this fallback. If any alphabetically earlier .fsl file in the workspace declares a symbol with the same name, go-to-definition jumps to the foreign file, and because `workspace_references` keys on `target_name` plus equality with that same (wrong) target, every same-named symbol in every file collapses into one identity. `textDocument/rename` then emits TextEdits into unrelated specs, i.e. a cross-file destructive refactor. Evidence status: UNVERIFIED — static reading only; no compiler, no test run. The in-file test `protocol_queries_project_one_authoritative_index` passes only because its two fixture documents share no symbol names (legacy.fsl declares Status/Order/status, queries.fsl declares ready/flip), and `refinement_targets_and_binders_resolve_without_workspace_guessing` asserts a local binder `u` resolves locally only because no sibling spec declares `u`; neither test exercises a collision. Requested evidence: a reproduction test with two workspace .fsl files each declaring a state variable of the same name, asserting that rename from within the alphabetically later file produces edits confined to that file. Unresolved: `crate::index` (DocumentIndex::definition_at / reference_at / symbol.owner) was not supplied, so the exact preconditions of `definition_at` could not be read.

Claim (issue_present): `alias_before_cursor` derives the qualifier token from `prefix.rfind('.')` over the ENTIRE document text preceding the cursor, with no bound to the current token, line, or even to a completion actually triggered by '.'. Any earlier dot in the file therefore selects an import scope for a completion request that has no qualifier at all. Concretely, an FSL import line `use Lib as lib from "lib.fsl"` contains a dot inside the path literal; for a cursor anywhere later in that document with no nearer dot, `prefix[..dot]` ends in `...from "lib`, `rsplit` on non-identifier characters yields the alias token `lib`, `index.import_for_alias("lib")` succeeds, and the completion arm at 286-295 replaces the current file's index with the imported file's index (`completion_index` shadowing `selected`). The user then receives the imported spec's members instead of the local ones. Evidence status: UNVERIFIED — derived by reading the string logic against the fixture literal in this same file's test `imported_definition_references_and_completion_cross_files` (main.fsl line 1 contains `"lib.fsl"` and alias `lib`); that test only asserts the positive case at Position(4,25) and never a cursor with no qualifier. Requested evidence: a test calling `alias_before_cursor(main, Position::new(2, 8))` (inside `state { n: Int }`, after the import line) and asserting `None`.

Claim (issue_present): there is no index or directory-listing cache anywhere in this file. `semantic_tokens` calls `definition_location` once per reference in the document; each such call runs `workspace_uris` (a full recursive `read_dir` walk of every workspace root, plus a sort) and then `index_for_uri` per candidate URI, and `index_for_uri` re-reads the file from disk via `source_for_uri` and re-runs `DocumentIndex::build`. Cost per `textDocument/semanticTokens/full` request is therefore O(references x workspace_files) file reads and parses plus O(references) directory walks; `workspace_references` (used by both references and rename) has the same shape with an extra `definition_location` per candidate reference, giving roughly O(files x references_per_file x files) parses. Semantic tokens are requested on essentially every edit, so this is an interactive-latency and IO-amplification defect, not merely a constant-factor one. Evidence status: UNVERIFIED — complexity argument from call structure only; no profiling, no benchmark, no execution. `DocumentIndex::build` cost was not read (crate::index not supplied), so the absolute cost per parse is unknown. Requested evidence: a timing benchmark of `semanticTokens/full` against a synthetic workspace (e.g. 200 .fsl files, ~50 references each) compared against a cached-index variant.

Claim (issue_present): the duplicate-write key (`init_write_key`) and the definite-assignment coverage (`assignment_coverage`/`Coverage`) use different granularities for the same statement, and the key is the coarser of the two. `init_write_key` only produces a `ConcreteIndex` for `LValue::Index` with a literal or non-binder `Expr::Var` subscript; every `LValue::Field` target falls through to `InitWriteKey::Root(root)`. Consequence A (false rejection): a straight-line init assigning two distinct fields of the same struct root, `p.x = ...; p.y = ...;`, produces `Root("p")` twice, so walk_init returns `state variable 'p' assigned more than once in init` and the model is rejected — even though `Coverage::Fields`, `join_coverage`'s Fields/Fields merge, and `coverage_is_full`'s per-declared-field check exist precisely to accept that program, and the doc comment at 346-352 states a struct root is fully assigned once every declared field has been assigned. That Fields/Fields join branch is unreachable for same-branch sequential writes for exactly this reason. Consequence B (missed detection, opposite direction): a `forall` binder subscript yields `Root(map)` while a later literal subscript yields `ConcreteIndex(map, "num:k")`, and a constant-named subscript yields `ConcreteIndex(map, "var:K")` while the numerically identical literal yields `ConcreteIndex(map, "num:k")`; overlapping writes to the same cell across those forms are not reported as double assignment. Evidence status: UNVERIFIED — read of this file only, no execution. `fsl_core`'s KernelLValue construction was not supplied, so whether the parser can actually emit two `Field(Var, _)` targets for one root in one init block is assumed, not established. Requested evidence: a unit test running `check_deterministic_init` on a kernel model whose init is `p.x = 0; p.y = 0;` for a two-field struct state root, asserting Ok(()).

Claim (issue_present): `result.states_explored` is only written at the end of a completed level (line 253) and at normal exit (261), but `seen` is grown inside the expansion loop (239). The early return on a step violation (220-228) therefore reports the `seen.len()` from the END OF THE PREVIOUS LEVEL, understating the states actually explored by however many children were discovered earlier in the current level; the budget return at 234-237 does refresh it, so the two early-exit paths disagree. The same early return leaves `max_frontier_width` and `action_coverage` reflecting a partially processed level while `depth_reached` is advanced to `level + 1`. `fsl-explicit` serializes `states_explored`/`max_frontier_width` directly, and this binary exists to be measured by a memory-ceiling regression test, so a stale count silently corrupts that measurement rather than failing loudly. Evidence status: UNVERIFIED — control-flow reading only; no execution, no instrumentation. Requested evidence: a test on a model whose violation occurs mid-level after at least one new child has been enqueued, asserting `states_explored == seen count` at return.

Claim (issue_present): the server keeps two independent, unsynchronized definitions of 'FSL keyword'. Completion offers the local `KEYWORDS` array (29-66); rename validation rejects reserved words via `crate::index::is_keyword` (823). They already disagree: this file's own test `rename_identifier_validation_is_closed` asserts `!valid_identifier("use")`, i.e. `is_keyword("use") == true`, yet `use` is absent from `KEYWORDS`, as are `from`, `internal`, `aggregate` and `refines`, all of which appear as syntax in this file's own fixtures. The observable effect is incomplete keyword completion today and unbounded drift between the two lists on any future grammar change, with only one side covered by a test. Evidence status: UNVERIFIED — `crate::index::is_keyword` was NOT supplied, so the full divergence set is inferred from one test assertion plus the fixture strings in this file; the `use` case is the only member established. Requested evidence: read `rust/fsl-lsp/src/index.rs` and diff its keyword set against `KEYWORDS`, or add a test asserting the two sets are equal.
